_comment: MapVibe poster-rendering PMTiles profile. Designed to preserve the OSM tag fidelity that python/mapvibe_render.py reads (highway tiers, railway types, water/parks geometry) rather than the typical web-mapping profile which collapses tag values for tile-size reasons. We are not bandwidth-bound — we are pixel-fidelity-bound — so simplification is conservative and tag preservation is exhaustive.

streets._comment: All road geometries. Lua keeps the raw highway= value as an attribute; Python's get_edge_colors / _CLEAN_HIDDEN_TYPES does tier filtering at draw time.
streets._simplify_rationale: Keep every node at z13+. Below z13 we tolerate ~10m simplification — invisible at the line weights we draw.

water._comment: Water polygons (natural=water, bay, strait, waterway=riverbank). Coastline accuracy matters visually — minimal simplification.

rail._comment: Railway lines (rail, light_rail, subway, tram, monorail). Lua keeps railway= value.

settings.name: MapVibe Poster Tiles
settings.description: Vector tiles tuned for poster-grade matplotlib rendering — full tag fidelity, conservative simplification.
settings._simplification_rationale: Web-mapping profiles simplify aggressively because their bottleneck is per-tile bytes over mobile data. Our reader is server-side; we range-fetch from R2 with zero egress cost. Larger tiles are fine. Geometry fidelity wins.
